item.title: NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as coordinator of its Anambra State campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The campaign council also features Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central; Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North; and Chief Ebuka Onunkwo, the party’s senatorial candidate for Anambra South. Other members include Emeka Kissinger Osisi as State Director of Youth Mobilisation, Barr. Ogechukwu Ekweozor as Director of Women Mobilisation, DIG Celestine Okoye (rtd) as Director of Security and AIG Innocent Ndubueze Anene (rtd) as Director of Election Monitoring and Vote Protection. The appointments were announced in a statement signed by the party’s State Director of Media and Publicity, Dr. Tony Onyima. The statement also named Chief Egwuoba Okika Innocent as Deputy State Coordinator, former Speaker of the Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, as State Chairman, and Barr. Paulinus Akabogu Izuchukwu as State Campaign Secretary. Campaign coordinators for the three senatorial districts are Hon. Kingsley Nwafor for Anambra South, Hon. Chuka Ezenwunne for Anambra Central and Hon. Chigbo Enwezor for Anambra North. All serving federal and state lawmakers elected on the party’s platform are also members of the campaign council. The council will operate through various directorates covering media and publicity, finance, logistics, women and youth mobilisation, security, grassroots mobilisation, election monitoring and vote protection, new media, protocol, policy research and documentation, and special duties. Onyima will serve as State Director of Media and Publicity, with Paschal Azubuike as his deputy, while Hon. Lady Azuka Enemuo and Mrs. Chika Ezeali will oversee finance as director and deputy director, respectively. The council also has coordinators for the 21 local government areas of the state as part of efforts to extend the party’s campaign activities to the grassroots. The NDC Anambra State Campaign Council is scheduled to be inaugurated on Wednesday, November 4, in Awka. The post NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has confirmed that the wife of former governor Peter Obi is the godmother of one of his children, months after a public disagreement over the relationship between their families. Soludo also disclosed that his wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi’s daughter, clarifying the family relationship that became a subject of public discussion in September. The governor made the disclosure in an interview with BBC News Igbo on Monday, describing Obi as a close friend and insisting that their families remained on good terms despite their political differences. “Peter Obi and I are good friends. Our two families are on good terms. His wife was the godmother of my child at baptism, and my wife was the godmother of his child at confirmation,” he said. Soludo explained that their differences were political, particularly over their preferences for who should govern Anambra State. He said he did not hold Obi’s political position against him, despite their disagreement over the state’s leadership. “I have a different vision of who should be governor of Anambra State. I am contesting, and he supported whoever he felt should be governor. I prevailed by the grace of God, and I don’t hold it against him,” the governor said. The post Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
item.description: Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country. Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said. The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances. He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties. According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources. “The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said. He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens. item.title: Tinubu Stepped In When Nigeria Was About To Collapse — Mutfwang
item.description: Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has called on Nigerians to exercise patience with President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the President inherited a country burdened by longstanding fiscal and structural challenges, and about to collapse when he assumed office in 2023. Mutfwang argued that the economic difficulties confronting the country did not begin with the Tinubu administration, insisting that Nigerians must consider the state of the economy at the time the President took over before assessing the impact of the ongoing reforms. The Governor stated this on Monday while inaugurating the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections at the Government House, Rayfield, Jos. Mutfwang Inaugurates 2027 APC Campaign Council He acknowledged the hardship occasioned by the economic adjustments but maintained that the reforms were necessary to address deep-rooted challenges, pointing to improvements in the country’s foreign reserves and fuel availability as indications of progress. Mutfwang urged Nigerians to give the reforms time to yield results, stressing that the country’s economic recovery required sustained commitment and an understanding of the challenges inherited by the present administration. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. The inauguration marked the commencement of coordinated mobilisation for the re-election of President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, as well as Governor Mutfwang, Deputy Governor Josephine Piyo and other APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats in Plateau State. The Governor also highlighted measures taken by his administration to ease the economic burden on residents, including the introduction of Tin City Metro buses, revival of rail services within Jos metropolis, a 50 per cent reduction in tuition fees in state-owned tertiary institutions and a 300 per cent increase in student allowances. He further acknowledged the benefits of the Federal Government’s student loan and scholarship interventions, which he said had supported Plateau indigenes studying in various universities. On security, Mutfwang admitted that challenges persisted across Plateau State but assured residents that his administration remained committed to protecting lives and property. item.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims, arrest 19 suspects
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours. The operations also led to the recovery of firearms, stolen valuables and motorcycles, while several attempted bandit attacks were foiled. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. He said investigations and follow-up operations were ongoing to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue more victims and recover stolen property. In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area. The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack. In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area. The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families. In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction. The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze. The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists. Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators. In Kano State, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad arrested five suspects accused of harbouring criminals in connection with the abduction of the APC Chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Fanka. Although the principal suspects reportedly escaped, the police recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles from the location. In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area after responding to a distress call. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye
item.description: The Deputy Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dino Melaye, has said a government led by Atiku Abubakar will not determine who becomes Senate President or Speaker of the House of Representatives. Melaye said the ADC would allow lawmakers to elect their leaders independently, insisting that the party was committed to democratic principles and an independent National Assembly. He stated this while answering questions on the oversight mechanisms the ADC would introduce to track government payments, fund releases and beneficiaries during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Monday. “To start with, an Atiku presidency will not determine who is going to be the Senate president, the president of the Senate, or the Speaker of the House of Representatives,” he said. “Atiku is a Democrat. ADC is a very democratic political party. So we are going to allow the people to elect their leaders.” Melaye argued that allowing lawmakers to choose their leaders would promote legislative independence and strengthen the National Assembly’s oversight of the executive arm of government. “And I told you that wherever you have the members electing their leaders, there is some modicum of independence,” he said. “So to start with, the ADC will make sure that the National Assembly is truly independent, and if the National Assembly is truly independent, that will drive their oversight functions over the Executive.” On the mechanisms for scrutinising government spending, the ADC campaign official said relevant National Assembly committees would be empowered to question government officials and monitor expenditure. He specifically identified the Committees on Establishment, Finance, and Budget and Planning as possible channels for investigating government spending and ensuring accountability. “The Committee on Establishment is responsible for questioning this type of spenders because they have direct oversight function over the State House. The committee on finance is there. The committee on budget and planning is there,” Melaye said. “So you can use any of these committees at least to ask questions.” The post 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the security arrangements around Cross River State Governor’s private residence in Calabar, following reports of alleged robberies in neighbouring homes. Atiku said residents of the estate where Governor Bassey Otu’s private residence is located had complained of repeated burglaries despite the presence of armed policemen and two roadblocks securing the governor’s property. According to him, one resident reportedly lost an air conditioner and a freezer to burglars, while another disclosed that two houses on a nearby street were attacked last week. The former Vice President disclosed this in a post on his X account on Tuesday, questioning the disparity between the security provided for the governor and the protection available to residents living in the same neighbourhood. He said the governor had been operating from his private residence for nearly three years while the Government House was undergoing renovation, yet residents living nearby remained exposed to security threats. “This is security, APC style: two roadblocks for the governor, and none for the people next door,” Atiku said. He questioned the capacity of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to address insecurity across the state, asking what it could offer communities outside the state capital if residents living beside the governor could not sleep without fear. Atiku also outlined his proposed security reforms, pledging to transform the Nigeria Police Force from what he described as a regime-protecting force into a citizen-focused public service. He said his administration would expand police personnel towards the international benchmark of one officer to every 450 citizens to improve security coverage across communities. The ADC presidential candidate also promised to establish community-based security and intelligence networks to enable neighbourhoods to identify and report threats before criminal activities occur. “Security that stops at the governor’s gate is not security; it is a fence,” he added. item.title: US Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island — Report
item.description: The United States on Monday attacked Iran’s Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The Journal, citing unnamed US officials, described the strike against Qeshm, the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession were heard on the island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. The Pentagon referred questions about the reported strikes to US Central Command, which did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment late Monday. The Journal reported that the US has been engaged in smaller-scale strikes against Iran for several weeks. It said some officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for oil shipments that has been largely blocked since the war began in late February. This picture taken by the southern Lebanese village of Zawtar al-Garbiya shows an Israeli excavator demolishing homes in the town of Zawtar al-Sharqiya on November 2, 2026. The paper said the US has not publicly announced the attacks, so as not to signal any intention of resuming major combat operations. On Monday, on the eve of midterm elections in the United States, Trump said that a deal with Tehran “could happen.” Oil prices, sent rocketing by Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor, plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the conflict. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence
item.description: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. item.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
item.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. item.title: WAFCON Victory: Tinubu Fulfils $100,000 Promise To Super Falcons
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled his $100,000 promise to the Super Falcons, following their historic victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), where Nigeria clinched a record-extending 10th continental title. ‎According to the National Sports Commission, the players have begun receiving payments of about ₦140 million, representing the naira equivalent of the $100,000 reward promised by the President after the team staged a remarkable comeback to defeat hosts Morocco in the final in July 2025. ‎The Super Falcons, who were trailing 2-0, produced a spirited second-half performance to stun the hosts and reclaim the African crown, further cementing their status as the continent’s most successful women’s national team. Super Falcons celebrate a goal at the WAFCON ‎Team captain, Rasheedat Ajibade, expressed gratitude to the President for fulfilling his promise, describing the gesture as a welcome recognition of the team’s achievement and contribution to Nigerian sports. ‎The payment is another demonstration of President Tinubu’s commitment to rewarding sporting excellence and motivating Nigerian athletes to achieve greater success on the international stage. The Super Falcons warming up ahead of a game. Photo credit: cafonline.com ‎The President had similarly promised and delivered $100,000 rewards to members of D’Tigress following their triumph at the 2025 FIBA Women’s AfroBasket, where Nigeria secured a fifth consecutive continental title. ‎The Commission commended President Tinubu for his consistent support for Nigerian athletes and for demonstrating that sporting excellence deserves tangible recognition. ‎The Commission added that the President’s commitment has strengthened confidence among athletes and sports administrators while encouraging a culture of reward, accountability and national pride. item.title: AI not enemy of democracy — Amupitan
item.description: THE Chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has defended the use of Artificial Intelligence in election management. According to him, the technology is not a threat to democracy, despite its potential misuse by malicious actors. Amupitan said AI could improve electoral administration through efficient voter registration, logistics planning, data analysis and the management of large voter databases. He warned that advances in generative AI had made it easier to create deceptive content capable of undermining public confidence in elections. The INEC chairman, who stated these at The Beyond the Ballot Summit in Abuja yesterday, explained that electoral management bodies worldwide had adopted AI-assisted processes to improve administrative efficiency and strengthen election planning. The INEC chairman’s remarks came amid preparations for the 2027 general election, with the commission recently announcing plans to integrate AI into Nigeria’s electoral system. He said: “Artificial Intelligence, AI, is not an enemy of democracy.” He, however, expressed concern over the growing accessibility of generative AI tools which, he said, could be exploited to manipulate voters and spread disinformation during elections. “However, the rabid democratisation of generative AI models has dramatically lowered the barrier to entry for malicious actors, capacities, capabilities that want to require speedy-level intelligence resources such as high voice cloning of public figures, hyper realistic synthesis of election officials making false announcements are now accessible at negligible cost. These tools target specific vulnerabilities with distinct timelines,” Amupitan said. The growing use of AI in electoral processes has heightened concerns about the spread of fabricated announcements, manipulated audio recordings and realistic videos that could mislead voters, impersonate public officials and disrupt election administration. While the technology offers opportunities to improve the efficiency of election management, its potential misuse presents challenges for electoral integrity, particularly in an environment where false information can spread rapidly through social media. INEC’s planned adoption of AI, therefore, places renewed emphasis on the need to balance technological innovation with safeguards against misinformation, impersonation and other forms of digital manipulation. The commission noted that it would ensure that the technology strengthened the credibility, transparency and efficiency of the electoral process as Nigeria approached the 2027 polls. The controversy over the use of AI in elections intensified recently after suspicious photographs, including images believed to have been AI-generated, were found in INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters. item.title: Nigeria needs leaders equipped for changing realities — Sam Adeyemi
item.description: By Ogochukwu Agha LAGOS—THE Senior Pastor of Daystar Christian Centre, Pastor Sam Adeyemi, yesterday, warned that Nigeria cannot afford leaders who learn on the job, lamenting that many occupying positions of authority have never received formal leadership training, despite the country’s mounting economic and social challenges. Adeyemi spoke in Lagos ahead of the 2026 edition of the church’s annual Excellence in Leadership Conference (ELC), scheduled for November 5 and 6, 2026, at the Daystar Christian Centre, Oregun in Lagos. Making a case for deliberate leadership development, he said: “Sometimes only God knows who is going to be governor. Who knows who is going to be senator tomorrow? And most people occupying leadership positions in our country have not learned leadership anywhere.” He urged Nigerians to take advantage of the conference, themed ‘Leading in Uncertainty’, describing participation as “a great investment in their lives. In a joint message, Adeyemi and his wife, Nike Adeyemi, who co-host the conference, said the event would explore “what it truly means to lead when the ground keeps shifting economically, socially, and personally. “Previous participants have described the conference as a game-changer, with some attributing practical improvements in their careers and businesses to lessons acquired at the event”, the statement reads. They explained that the theme was informed by prevailing realities, including volatile markets, rising living costs, policy changes and transformations in the world of work, against the backdrop of an approaching general election cycle. “Participants would be equipped to stand firm, think clearly, and lead boldly, while learning how to turn uncertainty into a leadership advantage,” they added. item.title: Five officers’ final duty in Zamfara
item.description: From Abdullahi Abdulrahaman Chakwa (Gusau), Salim Umar Ibrahim (Kano) & Dalhatu Liman (Abuja) Five police officers have been killed and several others injured in an ambush by bandits at Gidan Kano on the Gusau-Sokoto highway in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The officers were travelling in an 18-seater bus belonging to the Zamfara State Transport Authority when they were attacked on Monday morning. The security personnel were reportedly on their way to provide security during the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial rerun primary in Zamfara North Senatorial District when the incident occurred. A witness, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the bandits lay in ambush for the security operatives as they travelled along the highway. He said about five officers were feared killed, while several others sustained varying degrees of injury. “The bandits lay in ambush for the security personnel travelling in the Zamfara State Transport Authority bus. Five of them were killed, while many others were injured. The bullets penetrated the bus from different angles,” he said. However, another resident, who also spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, claimed that eight security personnel were killed, while several others were abducted by the gunmen. He said residents helped to evacuate the bodies of the deceased officers but could not account for some of the other personnel. “Eight security personnel were killed, and we helped to load their corpses into two different vehicles. We suspect that the remaining officers were abducted because they could not be found,” he added. In a related development, bandits ambushed workers of a telecommunications company at Tungan Tama village, along the same Gusau-Sokoto highway, a few kilometres from the scene of the attack at Gidan Kano. One person was reportedly killed, while several others sustained injuries in the attack on the telecommunications workers. “The bandits attacked them at Tungan Tama village, but they managed to reach Tashar Mayanchi, where we discovered that one person had been killed,” a resident said. Daily Trust gathered that bandits had carried out several attacks on communities along the highway, targeting travellers, residents and workers. The repeated attacks, involving road blockades, ambushes and kidnappings, have raised concerns about the safety of the strategic highway linking Zamfara State with Sokoto and other parts of the North-West. Commuters using the route continue to face the risk of being caught in attacks, while residents and motorists have expressed fears over the growing insecurity along the corridor. Police confirm attack on officers The spokesperson of the Zone 10 Police Command headquarters in Sokoto, ASP Abdallah Faruk Ambursa, confirmed the attack. item.title: Tinubu to unveil book on Olanipekun’s landmark cases
item.description: By Henry Ojelu LAGOS—PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will on November 19 unveil a six-volume publication documenting landmark cases handled by renowned legal practitioner, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN, over his 50 years in the Nigerian legal profession. The publication, titled ‘Wole Olanipekun through the cases’, examines Olanipekun’s contributions to the development of Nigerian law and jurisprudence through commentaries on significant cases he handled during his five decades at the Bar. The unveiling will take place at the WOC Justice Summit, an initiative of Wole Olanipekun & Co, which brings together stakeholders to deliberate on issues affecting the justice sector. The event will take place 24 hours after Olanipekun’s 75th birthday, having been born on November 18, 1951. The six-volume publication features forewords by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. It brings together contributions from retired judicial officers, academics, Senior Advocates of Nigeria and other prominent legal practitioners, offering an examination of the breadth of Olanipekun’s legal practice. and his influence on the country’s jurisprudence. The legal luminary is currently Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of the University of Lagos, having previously held similar positions at the University of Ibadan and Ajayi Crowther University. He is also Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Ajayi Crowther University and Chancellor of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology, Ikere-Ekiti. item.title: Osborne Foreshore drama: Lagos dep gov locked out by developer
item.description: *Residents accuse developer of canal encroachment, harassment By Godwin Oritse LAGOS—IN a dramatic development that has raised concerns over compliance with planning regulations in Lagos State, the Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, was reportedly locked out of a disputed construction site at Osborne Foreshore Phase II Estate, Ikoyi, on Saturday by Kenshad International Ltd, a developer facing allegations of planning violations and environmental infractions from residents. Hamzat, accompanied by a high-powered delegation of government officials and political leaders, waited for more than 30 minutes at the entrance of the development named Abba Court on Mahogany Close, but the gates were shut. The incident occurred during a visit prompted by complaints from residents, who accused the developer of engaging in unauthorised activities they said could threaten the safety and environmental integrity of the estate. “Why did he refuse to allow the Deputy Governor and his team in if he has nothing to hide?” a resident asked, expressing suspicion over the incident. The Deputy Governor expressed displeasure over the developer’s conduct and assured residents that the Lagos State Government would investigate the complaints. At a meeting with Hamzat tagged ‘Osborne Phase II residents and public leaders’ dialogue,’ residents accused the developer of constructing beneath high-tension electricity lines, constructing slabs over a canal, and carrying out sand-filling activities that have narrowed the water outlets in the estate. Speaking on behalf of the residents, Mr. Adebisi Taiwo alleged that the developer created an unauthorised back gate through which thugs were brought into the estate to intimidate those who questioned its activities. Taiwo also accused the developer of using security agents and unscrupulous officials to harass and intimidate them. The residents urged on the state government to investigate the allegations against Kenshad International and its owner and take appropriate action. “The developer had relied on a purported joint-venture arrangement with the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development to justify its activities. “The Lagos State Government must re-examine the arrangement and establish whether the project has complied with the applicable rules.” Responding to the complaints, Hamzat stressed that land use, physical planning and development control fall within the jurisdiction of state governments. Citing Supreme Court rulings, he argued that the Federal Government cannot simply assume the role of a state town-planning authority or issue building permits in place of the relevant state authorities. He pledged that the state government would look into the developer’s activities. Hamzat was accompanied on the visit by former Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Wale Edun; Senator Wasiu Eshilokun Sanni, representing Lagos Central Senatorial District; Hon. item.title: PAMA backs FG’s commitment to affordable long-term industrial financing
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Pan African Manufacturers Association (PAMA) has welcomed the Federal Government’s commitments to improve energy supply, provide affordable long-term financing for industries, strengthen local procurement, secure industrial corridors and establish quarterly engagements with manufacturers. According to the association, these priorities align with its broader commitment to advancing industrialisation, strengthening regional value chains and expanding intra-African trade. However, it stressed that effective implementation of the commitments would be critical to improving the operating environment for manufacturers, boosting industrial productivity and strengthening Nigeria’s competitiveness in regional and global markets. PAMA stated this while commending the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) for the successful hosting of its 54th Annual General Meeting (AGM). Held under the theme, “Leveraging National Industrial Policy to Position Nigeria as Africa’s Industrial Hub,” the AGM focused on implementing the Nigeria Industrial Policy 2025 (NIP 2025), enhancing manufacturing competitiveness, expanding access to industrial finance, reducing energy costs and promoting local value addition. A major highlight of the event was the 6th Adeola Odutola Lecture, delivered by Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, former Director-General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). Discussions at the meeting emphasised the need to translate industrial policy commitments into tangible economic outcomes through effective implementation, institutional accountability and sustained collaboration between the public and private sectors. PAMA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening partnership with MAN, noting that closer collaboration among manufacturers across Africa is essential to developing regional value chains, and expanding industrial capacity. and unlocking opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). It further emphasised the importance of building a competitive and integrated African manufacturing sector capable of driving sustainable economic growth, creating jobs and increasing the continent’s participation in regional and global trade. item.title: Procurement knowledge gap shuts small businesses out of FG contracts — Minister
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Many small businesses in Nigeria are missing out on Federal Government contracts due to inadequate knowledge of public procurement procedures, Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, has said. Enoh stated this in Abuja at the launch of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Public Procurement Training Programme and digital learning portal organised by the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), adding that limited knowledge, weak internal processes and inadequate capacity were hindering small businesses from competing effectively for government contracts. He said many entrepreneurs lacked the skills to register, meet compliance requirements, interpret procurement documents, prepare competitive bids and execute government contracts. “Many businesses are excluded because of capacity constraints, limited knowledge, weak internal processes and insufficient capability,” the minister said. Enoh added that some businesses were disqualified because of missing documents, while the complexity of procurement procedures further restricted their participation. He said the knowledge gap increased the cost of doing business and deepened small businesses’ dependence on intermediaries, stressing the need to give women-owned enterprises and other small businesses equal opportunities to compete. The minister urged business associations to publicise procurement opportunities and educate their members on bidding requirements. He also called on ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to simplify procurement procedures, improve transparency and strengthen support for small businesses. Director-General of BPP, Adebowale Adedokun, said MSMEs account for about 96 per cent of businesses in Nigeria and contribute approximately 50 per cent of the nation’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). He said despite their economic importance, many face barriers to public procurement, including inadequate technical knowledge and difficulties navigating bidding requirements, adding that the digital learning portal would provide free training tailored to Nigeria’s procurement system. item.title: AAUA bans signing-out ceremonies over security concerns
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The management of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA), Ondo State, has banned signing-out ceremonies and all related celebrations on campus over security concerns. The directive was contained in a circular issued by the Registrar, Dr Grace Olubunmi Babalola, dated October 30, 2026. According to the circular, the Vice-Chancellor, acting on behalf of the Senate, approved the ban in the interest of protecting lives and property within the university community. The management directed that no signing-out party, gathering, procession or other celebratory activity associated with the completion of academic programmes should be organised or held anywhere on campus until further notice. The directive takes immediate effect, with all students, particularly final-year students, urged to comply strictly. Deans, Heads of Departments, Heads of Units, security personnel and other relevant university officials have been directed to ensure strict enforcement and report any violation to the appropriate authorities. Babalola warned that students and other members of the university community who flout the directive would face disciplinary action in accordance with the institution’s extant laws and regulations. She added that cases involving suspected criminal conduct would be referred to law enforcement agencies for appropriate action. The Registrar urged members of the university community to cooperate with the management in maintaining a safe, peaceful and orderly campus environment, stressing that the suspension would remain in force until further notice. item.title: MAN convenes energy efficiency summit to boost manufacturing
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) is set to convene a two-day energy efficiency summit in Lagos to address high energy costs, improve industrial competitiveness and promote investment in alternative power solutions. Speaking in Lagos, MAN President, Dr. Ifeanyi Okoye, said the summit would bring together industry leaders, policymakers, regulators, technology providers and financial institutions to develop practical solutions to Nigeria’s industrial energy challenges. The summit, scheduled for November 3 to 4, organised through MAN’s power and energy subsidiary, Manufacturers Power Development Company Ltd (MPDCL), in partnership with the German Development Agency (GIZ) and Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP), will hold at Legend Hotel Lagos Airport, Ikeja, Lagos. With the theme, “Innovative Energy for Cost-Effective Smart Manufacturing with Structured Financing,” the event will focus on industrial energy security, efficiency and cost reduction. Okoye said high electricity tariffs, unreliable grid supply, fuel price volatility and dependence on expensive self-generation remained major constraints on manufacturers, undermining competitiveness, fuelling inflation and limiting job creation and Nigeria’s ability to maximise opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). He said: “To build a resilient, self-sustaining economy, we must address these challenges through a multi-faceted approach by expanding our energy infrastructure, accelerating energy efficiency adoption, diversifying industrial energy sources, and forging deep public-private capital partnerships.” Also speaking, MAN Director-General, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said previous summits had provided members with opportunities to engage solution providers, resulting in increased adoption of off-grid energy solutions by manufacturers. He said attracting investment was a major objective, noting that inadequate investment in the power sector and an unfavourable business environment had constrained capital inflows, particularly from foreign investors. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu’s Aide Refutes Claim President Visited Saudi Arabia To Get Northern Votes
item.description: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Foreign Affairs and Protocol, Ademola Oshodi, has dismissed claims that the President visited Mecca in Saudi Arabia to curry favour with northerners, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Oshodi, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, said the trip was strictly religious as the President is a Muslim. The aide said that Tinubu’s presence in Mecca was not political, adding that even an opposition governor, Bala Mohammed of Bauchi State, was also present as a Muslim. He advised other presidential candidates in the 2027 general elections to also seek favour from God. The presidential aide said that though Nigerians are going through hardship, Tinubu is working to make things better. The President arrived in Saudi Arabia on October 29 and performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. After completing the rites, he said that he felt fulfilled. Tinubu, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections, also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians.
